newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end off in year's lowest turnover.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end off in year's lowest turnover.

text.p: Brazil stocks closed slightly down in the thinnest volume of the year as today's U.S. Labor Day holiday kept most investors out of the local bourses, brokers said.
"The market was dead today," an analyst said. "There is nothing to comment on," he added, noting that trading was in the hands of a few market professionals.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most-active shares fell 0.43 percent, closing at 62,325 points. Market turnover totalled only 99.2 million reais ($97.6 million).

With Wall Street reopening Tuesday, local share prices are likely to move in tandem with U.S. bonds and stocks which fell in the last two sessions on mounting worries over a hike in U.S. interest rates, analysts said. ending at 75.40 reais, while its common share ended off 0.49 percent at 61.19 reais.
Mining giant Vale do Rio Doce preferred fell 1.78 percent to 19.35 reais.
State oil firm Petrobras preferred dropped 1.64 percent to 119.51 reais.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Electrical Energy Index closed up 1.83 percent at 1,573 points. The index comprises the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector.
